title: What sterling silver is
topic: sterling silver 92.5 percent silver 7.5 percent copper fineness 925 fine silver 99.9 soft hardness strength airborne sulfur silver sulfide black tarnish copper tarnishes faster

hook.text: Sterling silver is not pure silver.

lines.text: Sterling silver is not pure silver.
It is 92.5% silver and 7.5% other metal.
lines.say: It is ninety two point five percent silver and seven point five percent other metal.

lines.text: That is a fineness of 925 parts per thousand.
lines.say: That is a fineness of nine hundred twenty five parts per thousand.

lines.text: The other metal is usually copper.
Fine silver, 99.9% pure, is relatively soft.
lines.say: Fine silver, ninety nine point nine percent pure, is relatively soft.

lines.text: Soft silver scratches and marks easily.
So copper is added for hardness and strength.
But sulfur compounds in the air slowly turn silver black.
That black layer is silver sulfide.
Copper makes sterling tarnish faster than pure silver does.
So sterling is not pure because copper makes it harder.
A render shows how the metal looks before anything is cast.

post.caption: Sterling silver is 92.5% silver and 7.5% other metal, usually copper. Fine silver, 99.9% pure, is relatively soft, so copper is added for hardness and strength. Airborne sulfur compounds slowly turn silver black with a layer of silver sulfide, and the copper makes sterling tarnish faster than pure silver. The renders in this video were made with HeyGema.
